related_questions.question: How long does it take for a COVID test to show accurate results?
related_questions.snippet: NAATs tests are the “gold standard” for COVID-19 tests. Your sample will usually be taken by a healthcare provider and transported to a laboratory for testing and may take up to 3 days to receive results. Some NAATs may be performed at the point-of-care and provide results more quickly.

related_questions.question: How serious is catching COVID-19 now?
related_questions.snippet: Many people with COVID-19, also called coronavirus disease 2019, recover at home. But for some, COVID-19 can be a serious illness. Some people may need care in the hospital, treatment in the intensive care unit and the need for breathing help. In some people, severe COVID-19 illness can lead to death.

related_questions.question: How long from covid exposure do you test positive?

text_blocks.snippet: Generally, it takes 2-14 days after exposure for COVID-19 symptoms to appear, and you may test positive for the virus during this period. For the Omicron variant, the incubation period (the time between exposure and symptom onset) is typically around 3 days. Testing too early, before 5 days after exposure, can result in a false negative.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Symptoms can appear anytime between 2 and 14 days after exposure, according to the CDC.

list.title: Testing:
list.snippet: To get the most accurate results, it's best to wait 5 days after exposure before testing.

list.title: Omicron Variant:
list.snippet: The Omicron variant tends to have a shorter incubation period, with symptoms appearing around 3 days after exposure, according to WebMD.

list.title: False Negatives:
list.snippet: If you test too early, you may not have enough virus in your system to be detected, leading to a false negative result.
